Every graph's axes name a quantity and its unit (mA against %, m against min, °C against time of day, cm against cm), which is the repair for graph-as-picture (notes 6.5).

Each misconception the brief names for lesson 2 has a DO screen: graph as picture (the tank's falling stretch, step 6), the vertical line misapplied to a many-to-one curve (the workshop, step 8), a graph with a gap (the tariff, step 11).

fix: Causal step skipped: why going up from the input finds the output. Say the graph is built from pairs, each pair's dot sits straight above its input at the height of its output, so the upright beam finds the dot and the across beam reads its height. Show 0.16 × 25 + 4 = 8 as the rule the beam agrees with.

Causal step skipped: the circle is called a failure without the reason. Say one input, 3 cm, gives two outputs, 4 cm and −4 cm, so 'what does 3 cm give?' has no single answer; that is what the vertical line shows.
False absolute: 'the beam meets the graph once' fails where the graph has no point above an input (left of the tank's start, or a reading off the end of a line). Say at most once, at one height.

False absolute: 'if any vertical line meets a graph twice, it is not a function' needs 'drawn with the input along the bottom'. Also say the test is only a quick way of asking what each input gives, not a new rule, as the brief requires.
False absolute in ignores: 'real ones change smoothly'. Say a real level or temperature usually turns without a sharp corner.

Misconception not shown failing: graph-as-picture is stated but not shown. Add that a flat stretch is not a flat side and a falling stretch is not a slope; and say when a graph is a picture (both axes positions, as with the pipe's rim), so the belief is not called wrong where it holds.

The gap is asserted without its why, and the tariff and workshop graphs are missing from explain and whatAmILookingAt. Explain the filled and hollow dots (textbook convention) and why every time still has one price; describe the workshop's two straight pieces as the rule the readings come from.
Many-to-one: the workshop example, a level line at 22 °C meeting twice while every upright line meets once, belongs in explain so screen 8's answer is taught.
